chunks: My father narrated to me from Sa'd, from Ibrahim ibn Rayyan, who said: Yahya ibn al-Hasan al-Husayni narrated to me, who said: Ali ibn Abdillah ibn Qutrub narrated to me from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

His son passed by him while he was a young lad, and his sons were gathered around him. He said: 'This son of mine will die in a land of exile. Whoever visits him, submitting to his command and knowing his right, will be with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, like the martyrs of Badr.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Ali al-Rida (a.s.) according to Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the spiritual elevation of Imam Ali al-Rida (a.s.) by linking his burial in Tus to the prestigious status of the Badr martyrs, a comparison that underscores the merit of visiting the Ahl al-Bayt in their places of repose. The condition of 'recognition of their rights' (Haqq) reflects the Shia emphasis on gnosis (Ma'rifah) and loyalty (Wilayah) as prerequisites for receiving such high rewards.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 5. My father narrated to me from Sa’d, from Ibrāhīm ibn Rayyān, from Yaḥyā ibn Ḥasan Al-Ḥusaini, from ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Quťrub, who said:

One day when the children of Abil Ḥasan, Mūsā (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)), were gathered around him, his son (Imam Riďā (a.s.)), who was young at the time, passed by him. Imam (Kāżim (a.s.)) said: This son of mine will die lonely in a distant land. Verily those who go to his Ziyārah while submitting to him and knowing his rights will be regarded by Allāh, the Great and Almighty, as the martyrs of (the Battle of) Badr.
